EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows characteristic epoxide (oxirane) ring bands: a very intense line at 893 cm⁻¹ and companion bands at 812 cm⁻¹ and 582 cm⁻¹ match the strong ring breathing / deformation modes known for small epoxides (e.g. ethylene oxide Raman 883, 809, 575 cm⁻¹). A C–O stretching band near 1024 cm⁻¹ and CH-stretch group at 2888–2972 cm⁻¹ are also consistent with an aliphatic epoxide. The single strong C=O band at 1744 cm⁻¹ indicates an unconjugated aldehyde carbonyl, which candidate 3 (CCCC1OC1CC=O) possesses. Among the ten candidates, only molecule 3 contains an epoxide ring together with an aldehyde, matching all key spectral features; no other candidate explains the distinctive ~890 cm⁻¹ epoxide ring band.
